A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LLR-BC research, with matching authors, method, and core experiments. The complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, and appendices support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original CVRP and TSP lifelong-learning experiments, benchmark evaluations, component ablations, hyperparameter studies, and experiments with multiple base solvers.

after.justification: v3 retains those original experiments and adds evaluated comparators, ablations, non-lifelong comparisons, and analyses of confidence measures and buffer composition.

M1.justification: The proposed procedure retains final-epoch reservoir buffering, state-behavior experiences, variance-based CaEW weighting, reverse-KL consolidation, and the combined training loss. Algorithms 1–2 and Equations 1–2 are unchanged. The additional variants serve as ablation controls.

E1.justification: Both versions use CVRP and TSP with the same six synthetic distributions, scales 20/50/100, five task orders, and 42 CVRPLIB/TSPLIB benchmark instances. The added comparisons and analyses reuse this evaluation coverage.

E2.justification: v3 adds adapted Li (inter), Li (intra), and Feng baselines to the lifelong-learning and benchmark comparisons, retaining Restart, Fine-tuning, EWC, and LiBOG. New Tables 6–7 also compare POMO-MT-BL, POMO-MT-EL, and pretrained INViT. INViT previously appeared as a base solver in the applicability experiment; its standalone comparator role is new.

E3.justification: The original training budgets, test sets, and five lifelong-learning metrics remain. Added evaluations introduce batch-level and epoch-level multitask training, pretrained INViT testing, and task-specific Restart checkpoints. Tables 6–7 additionally report absolute distances and optimality gaps using HGS/Gurobi reference solutions. Appendix C.3 specifies new buffering and confidence-measure controls.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained component ablations and hyperparameter sweeps, v3 tests buffering every epoch, entropy and top-two-margin confidence measures, rebalanced reservoir sampling, and whole-instance buffering. Table 3 and Appendix C.3 also add variance–entropy correlation and per-task buffer-composition analyses, substantially expanding tests of the design choices.

E5.justification: Appendix C.3 introduces Pearson correlation estimation between variance and negative entropy over buffered experiences from one task-order-1 run, reporting 0.972367. The existing one-run-per-order design and mean/standard-deviation reporting remain unchanged; no additional seed replication or uncertainty intervals are documented.

E6.justification: v3 adds extensive baseline, ablation, distance/gap, and buffer-analysis results. Original Table 1 values remain unchanged, but the added Li variants achieve lower forgetting than LLR-BC. The instance-buffering ablation reports CVRP AP 35.4 versus 4.9 for the default, in Table 3's units. The new Li TSPLIB averages have conflicting method labels between Tables 2 and 10.

T1.justification: The computational-cost discussion corrects the ideal overhead estimate for |E| = 4 and problem scale 100 from 2% in v1 Appendix A.4 to 4% in v3 Appendix A.5, consistent with 4/100. Mathematical definitions, losses, and assumptions otherwise remain; no new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The central LLR-BC, CaEW, and DsBC contributions remain. The conclusion narrows applicability claims: lifelong learning across problem variants becomes future work potentially requiring task-specific components, and removing reliance on task identity becomes a possible reduction in that reliance.

C2.justification: v3 explains the Li baselines' lower forgetting through their allocation of training to past tasks, adds explanations for low-confidence decisions and alternative confidence measures, and interprets buffer imbalance as potentially appropriate for larger tasks. It also specifies how fixed replay sizes can impair small-task plasticity and large-task stability. These substantially expand the discussion of mechanisms and limitations.

D1.justification: Appendices C.1 and C.3 substantially expand implementation documentation: 200-instance task buffers and alpha = 0.5 for the new baselines, removal of Feng's fixed-size parameter, confidence normalization, and instance-buffering budgets. v1's EWC/LiBOG parameter-search description is dropped. The new reproducibility statement expands the promised materials, but code availability remains conditional on acceptance.

R1.justification: Five new references support confidence measurement, KL behavior, and cross-variant models. Comparisons with Li and Feng are elaborated, although much of this positioning already appeared in v1 Appendix A.5. Li's updated bibliographic entry refers to the same work.

P1.justification: v3 locally rewrites the introduction, replay explanation, and conclusion; redistributes the former novelty discussion; and adds reproducibility and LLM-usage statements. It also corrects wording and affiliation/contact details. The main narrative and section sequence remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: The comparison and ablation tables expand, Table 2 becomes two blocks, and new Tables 6–7 display distances and optimality gaps. Figures 3–4 and 12–15 are redrawn with additional methods, revised axes, and expanded legends. Figure 2 gains explanatory caption definitions, and several appendix displays are relocated.

improvement.justification: v3 addresses important evidential gaps in v1 by evaluating the closest lifelong-routing comparators and testing buffering time, replay granularity, and confidence-measure choices. Absolute distances and optimality gaps also make solution quality more assessable. These additions substantially strengthen the paper, although arbitrary baseline settings and removal of Feng's parameter limit comparative conclusions. Reporting still needs care: Tables 2 and 10 conflict on Li labels, and blanket stability-superiority statements remain despite the newly reported Li advantage in forgetting.
